summary: Limestone light on the St. Lawrence at Ogdensburg, built 1871 to replace an 1834 light; keepers to 1933; discontinued 1961; relit by its private owner in 2011.

lens.note: Fourth-order Fresnel lens from 1855 (LighthouseFriends); 270-degree Barbier & Fenestre lens from 1900 (NRHP)

structures.note: Raised to 65 ft in 1900 by brick extension; original 1834 dwelling replaced

access.note: Privately owned; not open to the public (USLHS)

events.note: First lighthouse: dwelling with lantern room, ten lamps and reflectors, erected later in 1834 (NRHP); the Digest gives 1835 for completion
Inspector found the river well above normal levels, cutting off the station by land; asked for seawall and foundation work
Fourth-order Fresnel lens replaced the lamps and reflectors
Congress appropriated $13,000 (15 July 1870): NRHP says for building a new light station; LighthouseFriends and the Digest say renovation and repairs; new-lighthouse work began the following month
New limestone dwelling and tower completed June 1871
Tower raised to 65 ft by brick extension; 270-degree lens replaced the 180-degree lens
Ferry Ferdinand ran aground on rocks in heavy fog near the light; passengers unharmed; boat later freed
Electric siren established at Ogdensburg Harbor (fog-signal change listed in the 1924 Bulletin)
Building unoccupied from 1942 (1946 account as quoted in NRHP); Digest says government stopped using it in 1942
General Services Administration sale; private bid of $2,400 accepted after the city declined to buy at $900 (property valued at $24,000)
Permit to demolish the building denied by the city: application lacked asbestos-removal plans and structural reviews
Relit by the private owner after Coast Guard certification as a private aid to navigation; the Digest dates it 8 October 2011, LighthouseFriends 7 October 2011 (private gathering; relit 8:20 p.m.)

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends: the light was discontinued on 1 June 1961. 1964 is the year the property was sold to a private owner (NRHP; LighthouseFriends).
USLHS place record gives the height of the light above mean high water as 63.5 ft (19.4 m).
The standing tower and dwelling date from the 1870-71 rebuild, completed June 1871 (NRHP). The 1834 light was the first, replaced by the new building.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The first lighthouse is dated 1834 by the NRHP and LighthouseFriends; the Digest gives 1835 for its completion. The story gives 1834 and notes the Digest's date. The standing building is the 1870-71 rebuild, completed June 1871.

The NRHP says Congress's July 1870 appropriation was for building a new light station; LighthouseFriends and the Digest say renovation and repairs (LighthouseFriends also says new-lighthouse work began the following month). The story states both and does not choose.

The 1900 Light-House Board report gives an increase of 20 feet; the NRHP gives the tower as 65 feet after 1900; LighthouseFriends and the Digest give the 1870 tower as 39 feet 8 inches. Those figures do not reconcile (about 60 feet if 20 feet were added). The story states them without choosing.
NRHP says his tenancy ended in 1911 but also places his resignation three years after the 1910 census (1913). The USLHS roster and LighthouseFriends give 1913. The story uses 1913.

NRHP: Cook caretaker to 1941. 1946 account (as quoted in NRHP): unoccupied since 1942. Digest: government stopped using it in 1942. LighthouseFriends: light discontinued 1 June 1961. The story reports each.
USLHS roster: Principal Lighthouse Keeper 1933-1941. NRHP and LighthouseFriends: caretaker. Recorded as role other, with a note.
NRHP (Gunn's tenure) and the 1924 Bulletin: oil to acetylene. Digest: whale oil to kerosene in 1875, kerosene to electric in 1924. The story gives both and does not adopt the Digest sequence.
NRHP: the city declined to buy the property valued at $24,000. LighthouseFriends and the Digest: offered to the city for $900 and declined. Both: a private bid of $2,400 was accepted.
The Digest gives 8 October 2011; LighthouseFriends describes a private gathering on 7 October 2011 at which the light was relit at 8:20 p.m. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Revised 2026-10-27 by the independent fact-check. Corrections made: the 1870 appropriation is now shown with both stated purposes (NRHP: new light station; LighthouseFriends and Digest: renovation and repairs), not as 'a new station'; the 2007 demolition permit was denied to an application made by a resident, not 'the owner' and not 'later' (the story now gives 2007 and does not name the applicant); Gunn is now 'Amherst E. Gunn', Hill 'Daniel D. Hill', Cook 'Harold M. Cook', as the roster prints them; the first-light date conflict (1834 NRHP vs 1835 Digest) and the relight-date conflict (8 October per the Digest vs 7 October per LighthouseFriends) are now stated; the tower-height figures that do not reconcile are stated; Penfield's 1911/1913 wording is clarified; footnotes 8 and 9 now carry the NRHP URL; footnote 5 gives the printed page (153), read from the OCR running head of the 1900 Light-House Board report, which has no scan-page index here; footnote 10 gives printed p. 24 (the Bulletin's PDF p. 22 was viewed as an image and reads 'fixed to occulting, oil to acetylene'). Copyright: the Lighthouse Digest and LighthouseFriends are paraphrased; only public-domain NRHP and Light-House Board or Bulletin text is quoted. Not read directly: the Jamestown Evening Journal (23 Jan 1922) and the Daily Argus (14 Dec 1946), both as cited in the NRHP nomination; the Watertown Daily Times 2011 item listed in the NRHP bibliography was not read. Living and private people: the private owners, later residents and the 2011 relighting party are not named (the Roethel family, the Montroy and Piercy tenants). The keepers named are pre-1945 public-service keepers from the roster and the NRHP. The record's characteristic 'Fl W 10s' is unverified; the story gives only occulting from 1924 (Bulletin). The record's focal height and the USLHS 'Active Aid to Navigation: No' are older than the 2011 relighting and were not used beyond the focal height in the corrections. The USLHS roster and the NRHP list the same twelve keepers; LighthouseFriends lists 'Samuel J. Sayre' and 'James E. Horton' the same way. The Digest says the relighting was done by Laurel Roethel, which the story does not name. The 1900 Light-House Board report entry is not dated by fiscal year beyond its title; the story says 'the fiscal year ended June 30, 1900', which matches the volume's title page.
